heroText: Tunis is Tunisia's Mediterranean capital, where a UNESCO-listed medina meets French-colonial boulevards and ancient Carthage just along the coast. First-time visitors should get lost in the Medina of Tunis's covered souks, admire the Roman mosaics at the Bardo National Museum, and stroll palm-lined Avenue Habib Bourguiba. Tunis–Carthage International Airport sits just minutes from downtown, making Tunis an easy gateway to both city sights and Mediterranean beach towns.

areas.name: Medina
areas.text: The Medina of Tunis is the historic walled old town, a UNESCO-listed maze of souks, mosques and artisan workshops best explored on foot.

areas.name: Ville Nouvelle
areas.text: Ville Nouvelle centres on Avenue Habib Bourguiba, Tunis's French-colonial boulevard lined with cafes, theatres and hotels.

areas.name: Les Berges du Lac
areas.text: Les Berges du Lac is a modern business district by the lake, home to newer hotels, malls and international offices.

areas.name: La Marsa
areas.text: La Marsa is an upscale coastal suburb near Carthage and Sidi Bou Said, popular for beach cafes and a relaxed seaside pace.

airports.name: Tunis–Carthage International Airport (TUN)
airports.text: Tunis–Carthage International Airport sits just northeast of downtown, a short taxi or metro-light-rail ride from the city centre.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Tunis–Carthage International Airport (TUN) and central Tunis before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in the Medina or Ville Nouvelle for an easy first stay near souks, museums and Avenue Habib Bourguiba, or choose Les Berges du Lac for modern business hotels. La Marsa suits travelers wanting easy access to Carthage, Sidi Bou Said and the coast.
hotelIntro: Tunis hotel choice depends on priorities: the Medina and Ville Nouvelle suit first-time visitors wanting sights within walking distance, Les Berges du Lac suits business travelers, and La Marsa suits those prioritising beaches and day trips to Carthage.
rentalCars: A rental car helps for exploring Carthage, Sidi Bou Said and the northern coast, though downtown Tunis is easily covered on foot, by taxi or the TGM light rail.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose the Medina or Ville Nouvelle for an easy first stay close to souks, museums and Avenue Habib Bourguiba.

travelTips.title: Medina navigation
travelTips.text: Expect to get pleasantly lost in the Medina's narrow lanes, and use landmark gates like Bab el Bhar to reorient.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Take a metered taxi or the TGM connection from Tunis–Carthage International Airport for the short ride into the centre.

travelTips.title: Carthage day trip
travelTips.text: Take the TGM light rail directly from downtown to Carthage and Sidi Bou Said for an easy half-day coastal excursion.

nearbyIdeas.name: Carthage
nearbyIdeas.label: Heritage
nearbyIdeas.text: The ruins of ancient Carthage sit along the coast northeast of Tunis, reachable by light rail for Roman and Punic archaeological sites.

nearbyIdeas.name: Sidi Bou Said
nearbyIdeas.label: Village
nearbyIdeas.text: Sidi Bou Said is a postcard-perfect blue-and-white clifftop village near Carthage, popular for its cafes and Mediterranean views.

history.label: 4th century
history.text: The existence of settlements in and around the area of Tunis is attested by sources dating from the 4th century BC.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Both the town and Carthage were destroyed; the former, however, was rebuilt first under the rule of Augustus and became an important town under Roman control and the center of a booming agricultural industry.

history.text: Under the Aghlabids, the city gained significance and benefited from economic improvements and became one of the most important in the caliphate, and was briefly the national capital from the end of the reign.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The governor appointed by Béjaïa, having reestablished order in the country, did not hesitate to free himself from the Hammadids to found the Khurasanid dynasty with Tunis as its capital.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The city became the capital of a Hafsid kingdom stretching towards Tripoli and Fez.
